paper_title: Iron Catalysis for Room-Temperature Aerobic Oxidation of Alcohols to Carboxylic Acids

questions.question: In this paper, what compound does the label "1a" refer to?
What is the chemical formula/structure given in the paper for the carboxylic acid product labeled 2a?
According to Table 1 and its footnote, what solvent and reaction time were used for the aerobic oxidation of aldehyde 1a to 2a?
questions.ground_truth_answer: Solvent: DCE (1,2-dichloroethane), temperature: room temperature; reaction time: 12 h under O2 (or 16 h when run with air) per Table 1/footnote.

questions.question: Which gave the higher yield for the oxidation of aldehyde 1a to acid 2a in Table 1: using O2 or using air?
questions.ground_truth_answer: O2 gave the higher yield: 94% with O2 vs 88% with air (Table 1, entry for 1a → 2a).

questions.question: What isolated yield (and mass, if reported) did the authors obtain for palmitic acid 2e from the large-scale (40 mmol) aerobic oxidation of cetyl alcohol 3e?
questions.ground_truth_answer: Palmitic acid 2e was obtained in 94% isolated yield (9.6817 g) from the 40 mmol oxidation of cetyl alcohol 3e (Scheme 3 / main text).
